sections.h2: What should a seller know about Tattnall County?
sections.html:
Tattnall County lies in southeast Georgia. Reidsville is the county seat and Glennville is the largest city, and the county was founded on December 5, 1801 and named for Josiah Tattnall. Wikipedia's county entry gives a total area of 488 square miles, of which 479 are land and 8.9 are water.

Three river systems divide the county. The west drains to the Ohoopee River, the northeast from Cobbtown to east of Reidsville drains to the Canoochee River, and the southeast and southwest corners drain to the Altamaha. Cities are Cobbtown, Collins, Glennville, Manassas and Reidsville, with Mendes as a census-designated place. U.S. 25 and 301 run together through the county, U.S. 280 follows State Route 30, and the neighbors are Candler, Evans, Liberty, Long, Wayne, Appling, Toombs and Emanuel counties.

The county's own website gives space to agriculture and the Vidalia onion, which tells you what keeps much of the land in use. The Census Bureau counted 22,842 people in 2020 and estimates 24,376 for July 2025, a rebound after a 10.5% drop between 2010 and 2020.

sections.h2: How do Tattnall County homes compare on the Census numbers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures put the median owner-occupied home in Tattnall County at $140,000, with 71.0% of housing units occupied by their owners. That sits above the $117,100 to $120,200 medians the Census Bureau reports for Talbot, Terrell and Sumter counties, while median gross rent is a lower $699.

Only 82.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is brisker than in the rural counties to the west, and the 28.1 minute average commute suggests many workers drive to jobs outside their own town.

sections.h2: Who handles Tattnall County property taxes?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner bills and collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors sets value. On the county's online payment site, the tax commissioner's office is listed at 108 West Brazell St., P.O. Box 920, Reidsville, GA 30453, phone 912-557-6736, open Monday through Friday from 8 to 5.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, collections, mobile home, public utility and timber taxes, plus vehicle tags.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: five members appointed by the county commissioners, with a chief appraiser who runs appraisal work.
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury to hear appeals of assessor values.
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set the budgets and millage rates that fund the bill.

The county's general information page says Tattnall's assessors have been delegated to receive tax returns, so returns and homestead applications go to the assessors' office. The state also levies a tax of no more than one fourth of one mill each year.

sections.h2: How do Tattnall County returns and exemptions work?
sections.html:
Returns for taxable property owned on January 1 are filed from January 1 through April 1. After the first one, the return renews automatically at the prior year's final value, and a new one is needed only when you add property, improve it or want to declare a different value.

Homestead exemption applies to a home you own and occupy as your legal residence, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's office. The county's pages give April 1 as the filing deadline, while its FAQ asks for applications before March 1, so file early. The Board of Tax Assessors page says no local homestead exemptions are offered, and owners apply for the statewide ones.

Special assessment programs are listed on the county FAQ:

  • Preferential agricultural property: assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40, held in current use for ten years.
  • Conservation use: current-use value for bona fide agricultural property, also a ten year covenant.
  • Environmentally sensitive and residential transitional property: current-use assessment under similar covenants, filed between January 2 and April 1.
  • Timber: not taxed until sold or harvested, then taxed on 100 percent of its fair market value.

Ask the assessors what a covenant means for the next owner before you list land that is enrolled.

sections.h2: When are Tattnall County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Read the due date printed on your bill. The state's county fact sheet for Tattnall says the official date is December 20, that a county may move it to December 1 or November 15 or use installments, and that every taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest accrues.

The county's online payment site has a property tax option next to its traffic ticket option, and the office phone is 912-557-6736. Mobile home owners follow their own state rule: a location permit within 30 days of placing the home, then a return and permit renewal between January 1 and April 1 every year.

One state credit is unsteady. The Homeowners Tax Relief Grant shows up as a credit on the bill only when the General Assembly funds it, and the county notes that the bill rises if the money is not appropriated. Ask the commissioner whether a credit appears on the current bill.

sections.h2: How does a Tattnall County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
When the assessors change a value, they send a notice, and the owner has 45 days from the date of the notice to appeal in writing. The county says late appeals are invalid.

An appeal rests on one of three grounds: taxability, uniformity or value. A complaint that the tax is too high does not qualify. The assessors review the appeal first, and if they make no change it is forwarded to the Board of Equalization, which holds a hearing. Either side can then go on to Tattnall County Superior Court. The taxpayer may choose arbitration in place of the Board of Equalization when filing.

The county also tells owners that assessors read the market and do not create value. If your closing price differs from the county's number, bring the contract to the assessors' office when you file.

sections.h2: What happens when Tattnall County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The county has held property tax sales at the courthouse, and one was set for Tuesday, June 7, 2022, at 10 a.m. in the Commissioners Meeting room on the second floor. A sale is the end of a long delinquency process, so a seller with a past due balance has options well before that point.

Ask the commissioner for written payoffs for every year. If the house is a mobile home, confirm the decal and permit are current as well. Georgia fixes fair market value as of January 1, and the county FAQ says property taxes are charged against the owner on that date. Settle the year's bill between buyer and seller on the closing statement, and have the title company pay prior balances from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Tattnall County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the tax commissioner at 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, or use the county's online payment site. The office phone is 912-557-6736, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8 to 5.

faqs.q: What is the Tattnall County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 is the deadline on the Board of Tax Assessors page. The county FAQ mentions March 1, so file before March to be safe. Applications go to the Tax Assessor's office.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Tattnall County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, and the appeal must be in writing. Late appeals are invalid.

faqs.q: Are there local homestead exemptions in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors page says no local homestead exemptions are offered, so owners apply for the statewide ones.
Yes, but only when it is sold or harvested. The tax is then based on 100 percent of fair market value, and the county FAQ describes lump sum, unit price and owner harvest sales.
